<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 49 pages)`
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f13af1dc014a8c6819c02500dda8f683bbabd108` — the merge of head `df622665dbdf34a43b0790ac4887404f7281a802` into base `ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f13af1dc014a8c6819c02500dda8f683bbabd108 && git checkout f13af1dc014a8c6819c02500dda8f683bbabd108
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f df622665dbdf34a43b0790ac4887404f7281a802 && git checkout -B drift-repro ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f && git merge --no-ff df622665dbdf34a43b0790ac4887404f7281a802

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ffd2cb6dad60dea5c001504c889831f969a869e9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.transfer-cascade-never-offered-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-transfer-cascades.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-transfer-cascades-36714.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, .changeset/transfer-cascade-lint.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Inputs read: card #36714 (body, triage 7102255110, claim 7177897953, dev report 7178906203, claim amendment 7180121254), the PR body, the net diff `origin/main...pr-37382` (13 files, +674/−4), and the 70 check-runs on this head (60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure; `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Test Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs` all success). Code outside the diff was read on `origin/main`, never reviewed: `packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts`, `packages/rest/src/change-owner-routes.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts`, `api-derivation.ts`, `injected-system-column-provenance.ts`, `field.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`, `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint`: narrowed. Right, and declared.** A stack that parsed and built before is now refused at `error` (tier `gating`, all three commands) in three shapes. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body, the changeset and claim amendment 7180121254 agree.
- **The refused set equals the runtime's never-offered set, for what a stack can decide. Right.** Read against `main`:
  - Case 1 (`transfer-cascade-parent-without-change-owner`): the cascade is reachable only through a Change Owner of the parent; both doors (`offeredDefinition` in core, the `GET …/change-owner/cascades` handler in rest) throw `403 CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED` when `changeOwnerOffReason(object, def)` answers, before `transferCascadeRelations` is called. The rule's `parentOffReason` is the same three-step function (`resolveUserActionTransfer(def).enabled` → `transferIneligibilityReason` → authored switch vs `controlled_by_parent` default), on the same spec predicates. No arm refused that the endpoint serves.
  - Case 2 (`transfer-cascade-extension-child-ineligible`): `transferCascadeRelations` drops a child when `transferCascadeIneligibilityReason(child) !== undefined`; the rule asks the same predicate of the served child. Limited to extension fields because `refuseIneligibleTransferCascades` already refuses the object's own fields at parse.
  - Case 3 (`transfer-cascade-child-update-unexposed`): the runtime filter is `canServeApiOperation(child.enable, 'update')`, defined as `apiExposureDenialReason(…) === null`; the rule calls `apiExposureDenialReason(childDef.enable, 'update')`. Identical verdict.
  - Field filter: `declaresCascade` is byte-for-byte the runtime's (`'cascade'`, `lookup` | `master_detail`, `multiple !== true`), and the parent is read through `referenceTargetOf` with the same try/catch.
- **No false refusal found.** Unknown objects are skipped on both sides (a parent or an extension target the stack does not declare), a `sys_` parent is left to `FieldSchema`. Authored vs registered shape: `transferIneligibilityReason` reads `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` / `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance`, which are documented and built to give one verdict for pre-injection and post-injection input (an absent `owner_id` and the platform's own definition both read as the platform anchor), and `ownerFieldDeclaredReadonly` reads both `fields` shapes, so judging the authored stack agrees with the runtime judging the registered definition. `ObjectExtensionSchema`'s merge carries no `userActions`, `ownership`, `managedBy`, `sharingModel` or `enable`, so no other package can flip a verdict except by adding a field, which `objectsAsServed` folds in for the stack's own extensions.
- **`fieldPatches` arm of the card's case 2 cannot occur. Right.** The patch shape refuses `transferBehavior` as an unrecognised key; a test pins it. The card's premise is narrower than written, and the PR says so.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/lint`: added** (`validateTransferCascades`, three rule-id constants, `TransferCascadeFinding`). Right, exported from the barrel beside its siblings.
- **`@objectstack/spec`: one data file** (the ADR-0087 semantic entry); no schema, no export, no generated artifact moves. Right.
- **`@objectstack/core`: one `CALLERS` row in a `.pin.test.ts`.** The package publishes `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` only; nothing ships. Right, and the row's classification (`not-a-served-read`, authoring-time static analysis) is true of the new caller of `referenceTargetOf`.
- **Wiring matches the siblings** (`validateAiContext` / `ai-context-*`, #37173): registry entry in `authoring-rules.ts` with `source`, `surfaces` and a `surfaceReason`; barrel export; one `os explain` entry per id in `rule-explanations.ts` and in `RULE_EXPLANATIONS`; the `second-object-read-exposure` pin row; the four CLI transcripts 79 → 80 (no fifth transcript carries the count).

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/lint` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor: right. The kind is `narrowed`, which takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves; both are moved, `@objectstack/core` is not (test file only) and is correctly absent.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right. No published accept set of the spec schema or public surface widens (new lint exports are additive API, not a metadata accept set); the authoring tools refuse what they accepted. The arm is on the PR body, the changeset body and the claim amendment.
- ADR-0087: the changeset carries exactly one marker, `registered transfer-cascade-never-offered-refused`, and the entry of that id exists in the diff. The FROM → TO and the one-line fix are in the changeset body (`Fix: set the field's transferBehavior to 'none' or remove it, or change the object the message names`).
- S1 (should-fix) — the changeset has no `**BREAKING**` banner and no `!` in its summary (`feat(lint): refuse …`). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` names the banner as a mandatory carrier of breaking-ness during the launch window, AGENTS.md calls `(narrowing)` BREAKING, and all twelve `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` changesets sampled on `main` carry it. The gate is green because the arm alone is a breaking signal, but the text that ships as `CHANGELOG.md` in two npm packages tells a consumer about the break only through a process token. Fix: `feat(lint)!:` and a `**BREAKING:**` lead on the paragraph that names the three refusals.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, file surface widened to `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`: accepted. `check:adr-0087-registration` requires the entry for `narrowed`; the claim's ⛔ was on schema changes under `packages/spec/src/**`, and this is ledger data. The amendment 7180121254 adds the core pin row to the surface; same judgment.
- Dev flag, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`: accepted for this PR, with S2 below. A Studio or MCP save of the three shapes still passes; the runtime stays safe because `transferCascadeRelations` re-judges.
- S2 (should-fix) — the crossing to the runtime publish gate is owed in three places (`surfaceReason`, the explanations' scope paragraph, the changeset) and no card number carries it. Until it lands, ADR-0049 holds at the CLI door only and the two doors disagree on the same document. The stated obstacle also looks weaker than written: `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance` is built to answer the same for an injected `owner_id` present in the registered definition as for one absent from the authored document, so the measurement is likely short. File the card and name it in the `surfaceReason`.
- Dev flag, an own-field cascade made ineligible only by an extension is not reported: see N1.
- Dev flag, transcript-count collision with #37354 / #37371: a queue-order matter, no contract effect; whichever lands second moves one number.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #35769 (row 7178935378)`: verified. The row exists on #35769 (open), names `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` and the three refusals, ordered after this PR merges. The skill paragraph on `main` stays true after this PR (it lists the parse refusals); it is incomplete, not wrong.
- Dogfood battery on the final head (owed by the amendment): `Dogfood Regression Gate` success on this head.
- No `open_questions` on the card or the report.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The rule reads metadata only; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it takes no declared capability away. `transferBehavior: 'cascade'` keeps every case in which the Change Owner endpoint acts on it; the three refused shapes are ones the endpoint already drops on every call, silently. The rule makes the spec's own contract (liveness row `transferBehavior`: "offers and runs only declared single-value cascades whose child offers Change Owner") real at author time, which is what ruling 7000907189 point 4 ("parse or lint") and ADR-0049 ask. `error` is the right severity: each verdict is decidable from the stack, and the object's-own-field half of case 2 is already a parse error, so a warning here would grade the same mistake two ways.

- `packages/lint/src/validate-transfer-cascades.ts` against `change-record-owner.ts`: agrees, as ① sets out. The file imports the predicates and holds only the walk, so the two cannot drift by re-implementation; the remaining drift surface is the walk's field filter, which is the runtime's.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.transfer-cascade-never-offered-refused.ts` against the rule: `surface` lists every arm `transferIneligibilityReason` has plus both switch-off origins, both extension and own-field carriers, and both exposure reasons; `replacement` names the three ids; the acceptance route `GET /api/v1/data/PARENT/change-owner/cascades` is the registered route. "No mechanical rewrite" is right: dropping the cascade and changing the object are different intents.
- `rule-explanations.ts`: the three entries state where the verdicts come from, what is skipped and that the publish gate does not run them yet. Accurate against the code.
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`: the added sentence is accurate and sits beside the existing multi-value refusal.
- N1 (nit) — a cascade on a field the object declares itself, on an object that is eligible as authored but ineligible as served (an in-stack extension declares `owner_id` `readonly: true` on it, or the like), is refused by neither the parse (authored object is eligible) nor case 2 (extension fields only), and the runtime never offers it. Exotic, disclosed, runtime-safe. The served child is already in hand at that point: judging every site against it and reporting a non-extension site only when the authored object passes would close it.
- N2 (nit) — the test pins four of the parent arms (`org`, `none`, `managedBy`, switch off) and the `controlled_by_parent` default. `business_unit`, `systemFields: false`, a readonly `owner_id`, an unprovable external owner and the object form `userActions.transfer: { enabled: false }` are covered only through the shared predicate's own tests. Enough for the contract; a row for the readonly `owner_id` arriving through an extension would also pin the served-object read on the parent side.
- N3 (nit) — `parent !== undefined &&` in the case-1 condition is redundant (`parentReason` is defined only when `parentDef` is, which requires `parent`).

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are text and a card; neither changes what the rule refuses.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `ffd2cb6dad`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: the two should-fix findings of contract record 7180267565 are fixed in this PR before landing, and the dogfood battery is read on the final head; the rest of L1 reads clean.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 13 files (+674/−4), `Fixes #36714`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (amendment 7180121254). `l1-face` flags two items:
   - `changeset` on `@objectstack/core` is a false positive: the only core file is `second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, which ships nothing.
   - `dogfood` is owed on the final head. The battery passed at `8737482b`, and the refreshed os-dev-report at the final head is still due.
2. **Premise**: the record finds the rule refuses exactly what the Change Owner runtime on `main` never offers, and no false refusal. Case 1 shares `changeOwnerOffReason`, case 2 shares `transferCascadeIneligibilityReason`, and case 3 is `apiExposureDenialReason` behind `canServeApiOperation`. The rule is wired like the `ai-context-*` siblings.
3. **Owed in this PR**:
   - **S1.** The changeset carries no `**BREAKING**` banner and no `!` in its summary. Every narrowing changeset on `main` carries the banner, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` names it as a carrier. Add it.
   - **S2.** The crossing to the runtime publish gate (`surfaces: CLI_ONLY`, so Studio and MCP saves still accept the three shapes) is owed in three places and has no card. The area files that follow-up under #36714, and the three places cite its number. Note the record's reading: the provenance predicate is built to be stable across injection, so the obstacle may be smaller than the text says.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: contract nits N1 (an own-field cascade made ineligible only by an in-stack extension, disclosed, runtime safe), N2 (the five unpinned parent arms, covered by the shared predicate's tests) and N3 (a redundant `parent !== undefined`).
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: Skills-docs follow-up row 7178935378 on #35769. The publish-gate crossing goes to the card S2 asks for.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier, `Security-touching: yes`. A same-head at-tier PASS with S1 and S2 closed, a `dogfood_battery` on that head in the os-dev-report, and an **ACCEPT** are owed. The area lands it.
